rows.why: S1 covers several list items: the BOM (1), CRLF on every row including the last (2), the header (3) and row order (5). Item 3 is the closest because the scenario is mainly about the header row. Its pick writes exactly 'Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created'. The other three picks also match the scenario.

S2 sets how values are shown to people. No list item asks how status is labelled. Item 6 asks how the creation time is formatted, which is the closest fit. The scenario wants the UTC date as YYYY-MM-DD, but the pick writes a full ISO timestamp with milliseconds. Item 8 (missing title gives an empty field) also fits part of S2 and agrees.
Item 4 asks what an empty list produces. Its pick is the BOM and header line only, which is what S3 expects.
Item 7 asks how fields that need quoting are written. Its pick quotes only for a comma, quote, CR or LF. S4 also quotes a field that starts or ends with a space, which the pick would leave unquoted.
No list item asks about titles that start like a formula ('=', '+', '-', '@', tab, CR) or about adding a leading single quote. Item 7 is only about quoting.

Items 9, 10 and 11 each cover one way a requisition can be invalid, and none covers an invalid creation time. Item 12 is the closest because it asks the scenario's overall question: does the export fail or skip the bad row? Its pick makes the whole build throw, which matches 'building fails'. Items 9 to 11 add that the error names the requisition id, also matching S6.
